title: Company Census File (dataset az4n-8mr2), queried via Socrata API
claim: 8-county Chicago area (Cook, DuPage, Will, Lake, Kane, McHenry, Kendall, Grundy), status=Active: 36,851 carriers; 25,049 with MCS-150 updated 2024+. Of those recent filers: 17,611 carriers with 1-5 power units (30,228 PU); 5,288 with 6-100 PU (120,820 PU; 4,442 for-hire, 842 private-only); the 6-100 PU group reports 52,879 owned + 42,998 term-leased trailers, 47,221 owned tractors, 16,776 owned straight trucks; 3,325 carriers (2+ PU) flag construction cargo, 824 utility, 1,261 hazmat; 981 intrastate-only carriers with 2+ PU. Illinois statewide: 56,206 active carriers; 7,259 recent filers with 6-100 PU (152,915 PU). Top cities (6-100 PU): Chicago 535, Schaumburg 177, Naperville 169, Plainfield 160, Aurora 138, Elk Grove Village 134.
excerpt: Contains records for active, inactive, and pending entities registered with FMCSA... equipment and driver data (dataset description, paraphrased).
limitations: Self-reported MCS-150 data; 'Active' includes stale registrations (hence the 2024+ filter); power-unit sums are inflated by misreported outliers (e.g., Kendall County shows 84,701 PU for 581 carriers), so carrier counts by size bucket are more reliable than PU totals. Government fleets and non-registered light vans (e.g., most last-mile cargo vans <10,001 lb) are largely absent. Office address may differ from where trucks are parked.

title: 49 CFR 396.17 Periodic inspection
claim: Every CMV (each unit of a combination incl. trailers/dollies) must pass a periodic inspection at least once in the preceding 12 months with documentation on the vehicle; carriers may self-inspect or use a commercial garage/fleet leasing company as agent employing qualified inspectors; intermodal equipment providers must inspect interchanged equipment; State periodic inspection programs meeting Appendix A count as equivalent.
excerpt: ...has passed an inspection in accordance with the terms of this section at least once during the preceding 12 months and documentation of such inspection is on the vehicle.
limitations: eCFR.gov blocked automated access; text taken from Cornell's reproduction; amendment dates per Cornell.

title: 49 CFR 396.19 Inspector qualifications
claim: Annual inspectors qualify via a Federal/State-sponsored training program or state certificate, or at least 1 year combined training/experience (e.g., mechanic at a commercial garage/fleet); carriers must retain evidence of inspector qualifications. No license is required.
excerpt: Have a combination of training or experience totaling at least 1 year.
limitations: Federal rule only; Illinois overlays its own periodic safety-test regime (see S007/S008).

title: 49 CFR 391.51 General requirements for driver qualification files
claim: Each motor carrier must maintain a driver qualification file per driver: application, MVRs from each licensing state, road test certificate, annual MVR inquiry and annual review note, medical examiner's certificate/CDLIS record, etc. Creates recurring administrative workload for every carrier.
excerpt: Each motor carrier shall maintain a driver qualification file for each driver it employs.
limitations: Does not quantify cost of compliance or outsourcing spend.

title: 49 CFR 382.701 Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse queries
claim: Employers must run a full pre-employment Clearinghouse query and at least an annual query (limited query permitted with driver consent) for every driver subject to testing; a hit on a limited query requires a full query within 24 hours.
excerpt: Employers must conduct a query of the Clearinghouse at least once per year for information for all employees subject to controlled substance and alcohol testing.
limitations: Query fees and C/TPA designation mechanics not retrieved (fmcsa.dot.gov returned 403).

title: 49 CFR 382.305 Random testing
claim: Baseline minimum annual random testing rates: 10% of average driver positions for alcohol and 50% for controlled substances; FMCSA Administrator may adjust annually based on industry violation rates.
excerpt: the minimum annual percentage rate for random controlled substances testing shall be 50 percent of the average number of driver positions.
limitations: The rate actually in force for calendar 2026 was not verified (FMCSA notice not retrievable).

title: Vehicle inspections (Commercial Vehicle Safety Section)
claim: Second-division vehicles operated in Illinois must be periodically safety inspected; ~200 Official Testing Stations handle periodic/school bus inspections and ~260 handle truck, trailer and rebuilt inspections; school buses every 6 months or 10,000 miles; intrastate diesel vehicles >16,000 lb registered in Cook, DuPage, Kane, Lake, McHenry, Will (and others) and 2+ model years old are subject to diesel emissions testing.
excerpt: Second division vehicles operated on Illinois highways must be inspected on a periodic basis under established criteria (paraphrase of page).
limitations: Page gives no fee schedule, no weight thresholds for trucks, and no data on test prices charged by stations; station counts are approximate and differ between IDOT pages.

organization: Cornell LII (Ill. Admin. Code tit. 92, Part 451 - Official Testing Stations)
title: 92 Ill. Adm. Code 451.70 Official Testing Station permit requirements
claim: OTS permits issued as Public (must inspect any vehicle presented) or Private (not open to public; solely for testing 75+ vehicles owned/leased by the permit holder; inspections inside the OTS building); applicant files a $1,000 surety bond; each station needs at least one Certified Safety Tester (CST); permit is location-specific; this version shows a $10 application fee.
excerpt: They are established solely for the purpose of testing 75 or more vehicles owned or leased by the firm in whose name the Official Testing Station Permit is issued.
limitations: Cornell copy may lag the current JCAR text; a search-engine summary of the current ILGA text indicated a $50 application/$50 renewal fee and new OTS dimension requirements effective July 1, 2025 (ilga.gov returned 503, not directly verified). Test prices charged to customers not regulated/published here.

title: Illinois Auto Dealer License guide
claim: Illinois used vehicle dealer license: required for selling, dealing or brokering 5+ vehicles/yr; $1,000 fee (lower if filed late in year; deadline stated inconsistently June 1/June 15); $50,000 surety bond; established place of business (not a residence; site inspection; open 4 consecutive hrs, 5 days/week); 8-hour dealer training; Live Scan background check; liability insurance minimums; annual Dec 31 expiry.
excerpt: selling, dealing, or brokering five or more vehicles per year.
limitations: Secondary commercial source with internal date inconsistency; statute text (625 ILCS 5/5-102) could not be retrieved directly because ilga.gov returned 503; a search-engine excerpt of 5-101 indicated a $500 fee for applications after June 15 and $50,000 bond per used-dealer location.

title: Illinois Vehicle Code 5-102 Used vehicle dealers must be licensed
claim: Statutory basis for used vehicle dealer licensing via the Secretary of State (application verified by oath; fees refundable only on denial).
excerpt: An application for a used vehicle dealer's license shall be filed with the Secretary of State, duly verified by oath (via search excerpt).
limitations: Page returned HTTP 503 at access; content known only from search-engine excerpts; fee/bond amounts therefore rely on S009 (D).

title: Illinois Vehicle Code 5-301 Automotive parts recyclers, scrap processors, repairers and rebuilders must be licensed
claim: Dismantling vehicles for parts (automotive parts recycler), scrap processing and rebuilding salvage vehicles require Secretary of State licensing; repairers/rebuilders face extra requirements (workers' comp classification, sales-tax registration).
excerpt: Automotive parts recyclers, scrap processors, repairers and rebuilders must be licensed (section heading).
limitations: Full text and current fee not retrieved (ilga.gov 503); details from search excerpts of current and 2005 text.

title: Illinois Secretary of State - Vehicle Services - Dealer/Remitter Licensing Section
claim: Illinois SOS operates a combined Dealer/Remitter Licensing Section (remitters = licensed third parties that process title/registration); lists $1,000 certificate of authority fee for dealers and $50 per additional used-dealer location.
excerpt: $1000 certificate of authority fee (via search excerpt).
limitations: Secondary aggregator; remitter license requirements, bond and permissible fees NOT found (MISSING).

organization: Cornell LII (40 CFR 122.34, EPA NPDES small MS4 permit requirements)
title: 40 CFR 122.34 Permit requirements for regulated small MS4s (illicit discharge detection and elimination)
claim: Small MS4 permits must require municipalities to effectively prohibit, via ordinance, non-stormwater discharges into the storm sewer; the list of allowable non-stormwater flows includes 'individual residential car washing' but not commercial/fleet washing, so mobile fleet wash water must be captured and lawfully disposed (e.g., sanitary sewer with POTW approval or hauled).
excerpt: effectively prohibit, through ordinance, or other regulatory mechanism, non-storm water discharges into the storm sewer system
limitations: Federal framework only; Chicago is largely a combined-sewer system and MWRD/municipal sewer-use rules for mobile wash water were NOT retrieved (MISSING); Illinois EPA general MS4 permit text not retrieved.

organization: Cornell LII (29 CFR 1910.178, OSHA powered industrial trucks)
title: 29 CFR 1910.178 Powered industrial trucks
claim: Forklifts must be examined before being placed in service at least daily (after each shift if round-the-clock), and defects corrected before use; operator performance evaluation at least once every three years.
excerpt: Industrial trucks shall be examined before being placed in service... Such examination shall be made at least daily.
limitations: Mandates daily examination by the employer, not third-party PM; PM frequency is OEM-recommended, not regulated.

organization: Cornell LII (29 CFR 1926.1412, OSHA cranes & derricks in construction)
title: 29 CFR 1926.1412 Inspections
claim: Construction cranes require an annual/comprehensive inspection at least every 12 months by a qualified person (disassembly as necessary), in addition to shift and monthly inspections.
excerpt: at least every 12 months, the equipment must be inspected by a qualified person.
limitations: Aerial lift (ANSI A92) annual inspection standards are paywalled and not retrieved; Chicago/Illinois crane-specific licensing not checked (MISSING).

title: 49 CFR 390.5 Definitions - Commercial motor vehicle
claim: A CMV for FMCSR purposes includes vehicles with GVWR/GCWR of 10,001 lb or more used in interstate commerce, or designed to carry 9+ passengers for compensation; most last-mile cargo vans fall below this threshold.
excerpt: Has a gross vehicle weight rating or gross combination weight rating... of 4,536 kg (10,001 pounds) or more.
limitations: Definition only.

organization: LKQ Corporation (SEC Form 10-K FY2025, plus XBRL companyfacts)
title: LKQ Corporation Annual Report on Form 10-K for fiscal 2025
claim: Incumbent economics: FY2025 revenue $13,651M, gross profit $5,265M (38.6%), operating income $993M (7.3%), net income $608M, operating cash flow $1,063M. Procures salvage by buying total-loss vehicles at regional salvage auctions; notes limited salvage supply and rising bidder competition; EVs lack engines/transmissions, which are among its largest North America SKUs; provides mobile/remote diagnostics (Elitek) and hybrid battery reconditioning/installation (Green Bean Battery).
excerpt: Electric vehicles do not have traditional engines, transmissions, and certain related parts.
limitations: Mature global incumbent with scale purchasing; margins are not new-entrant economics.

organization: Copart, Inc. (SEC Form 10-K FY ended 2026-07-31, plus XBRL)
title: Copart Annual Report on Form 10-K fiscal 2026
claim: Incumbent economics: FY2026 revenue $4,666M, operating income $1,653M (~36% of revenue per 10-K table), net income $1,484M, operating cash flow $1,604M, capex $337M; service revenues 85% of total; sells mainly insurer total-loss vehicles to licensed dismantlers, rebuilders, dealers, exporters and public; opened a Chicago, Illinois location May 2025; owns Purple Wave (online equipment auctions).
excerpt: We sell the vehicles principally to licensed vehicle dismantlers, rebuilders, repair licensees, used vehicle dealers, exporters, and to the general public.
limitations: Two-sided network-effect incumbent; its margins are unattainable for a new entrant.

organization: RB Global, Inc. (SEC XBRL companyfacts from FY2025 10-K)
title: RB Global FY2025 financial data (10-K filed 2026-02-25)
claim: Incumbent economics (Ritchie Bros + IAA): FY2025 revenue $4,591M, operating income $713M (15.5%), net income $428M, operating cash flow $978M, capex $259M.
excerpt: Revenues 4,591M; OperatingIncomeLoss 713M (XBRL values, FY2025).
limitations: XBRL figures only; segment detail (commercial assets vs automotive) not extracted.

organization: Genuine Parts Company (SEC Form 10-K FY2025, plus XBRL)
title: Genuine Parts Company Annual Report on Form 10-K for fiscal 2025
claim: Incumbent economics: FY2025 revenue $24,300M, gross profit $8,941M (36.8%), net income $66M (vs $904M in 2024, depressed by charges); operating cash flow $891M. Management cites miles driven, an aging vehicle fleet, vehicle complexity and 'expanding opportunities in electric and hybrid vehicles' as aftermarket growth drivers.
excerpt: growth is driven by increases in miles driven, a growing and aging vehicle fleet, rising complexity in vehicle technology
limitations: Consolidated (automotive + industrial); 2025 net income distorted by one-time items not analyzed here.

organization: Rush Enterprises, Inc. (SEC Form 10-K FY2025, plus XBRL)
title: Rush Enterprises Annual Report on Form 10-K for fiscal 2025
claim: Commercial-truck dealer benchmark: FY2025 revenue $7,434M, gross profit $1,461M (19.7%), operating income $394M (5.3%). Aftermarket Products & Services revenue $2,523.2M with gross profit $930.5M (~36.9%); parts gross margins historically 28-30%, service & collision 66-68%; absorption ratio 130.7%; 3,733 vehicles under contract maintenance; uses mobile service units and technicians stationed at customer facilities; new Class 8 gross margin fell to 8.6% (freight recession); used truck units -1.9%; flags EV drivetrains as a risk to parts/service (fewer parts) and notes EPA moves to repeal its GHG endangerment finding.
excerpt: Historically, parts operations' gross margins range from 28% to 30% and service and collision center operations range from 66% to 68%.
limitations: Dealer-scale incumbent with OEM franchises and warranty work; service gross margin excludes overhead; not new-entrant economics.

organization: Ryder System, Inc. (SEC Form 10-K FY2025, plus XBRL)
title: Ryder System Annual Report on Form 10-K for fiscal 2025
claim: Fleet-services benchmark: FY2025 revenue $12,665M, pretax income $685M, net income $499M. Fleet Management Solutions total revenue $5,845M with FMS EBT $501M (8.6%); ChoiceLease 60% of FMS revenue; 'SelectCare and other' (maintenance for vehicles customers own/lease elsewhere) $680M; 20% of operating locations are at customer sites; offers on-demand retail mobile maintenance (Torque by Ryder) in select markets.
excerpt: We also offer on-demand retail mobile maintenance in select U.S. markets... through our Torque by Ryder service offering.
limitations: Capital-intensive lessor; EBT margin reflects leasing balance sheet, not a service-only entrant.
